781: /* This function returns an SDS string representing the specified selector ACL
782:  * rules related to command execution, in the same format you could set them
783:  * back using ACL SETUSER. The function will return just the set of rules needed
784:  * to recreate the user commands bitmap, without including other user flags such
785:  * as on/off, passwords and so forth. The returned string always starts with
786:  * the +@all or -@all rule, depending on the user bitmap, and is followed, if
787:  * needed, by the other rules needed to narrow or extend what the user can do. */
788: sds ACLDescribeSelectorCommandRules(aclSelector *selector) {
789:     sds rules = sdsempty();
790: 
791:     /* We use this fake selector as a "sanity" check to make sure the rules
792:      * we generate have the same bitmap as those on the current selector. */
793:     aclSelector *fake_selector = ACLCreateSelector(0);
794: 
795:     /* Here we want to understand if we should start with +@all or -@all.
796:      * Note that when starting with +@all and subtracting, the user
797:      * will be able to execute future commands, while -@all and adding will just
798:      * allow the user the run the selected commands and/or categories.
799:      * How do we test for that? We use the trick of a reserved command ID bit
800:      * that is set only by +@all (and its alias "allcommands"). */
801:     if (ACLSelectorCanExecuteFutureCommands(selector)) {
802:         rules = sdscat(rules,"+@all ");
803:         ACLSetSelector(fake_selector,"+@all",-1);
804:     } else {
805:         rules = sdscat(rules,"-@all ");
806:         ACLSetSelector(fake_selector,"-@all",-1);
807:     }
808: 
809:     /* Apply all of the commands and categories to the fake selector. */
810:     int argc = 0;
811:     sds *argv = sdssplitargs(selector->command_rules, &argc);
812:     serverAssert(argv != NULL);
813: 
814:     for(int i = 0; i < argc; i++) {
815:         int res = ACLSetSelector(fake_selector, argv[i], -1);
816:         serverAssert(res == C_OK);
817:     }
818:     if (sdslen(selector->command_rules)) {
819:         rules = sdscatfmt(rules, "%S ", selector->command_rules);
820:     }
821:     sdsfreesplitres(argv, argc);
822: 
823:     /* Trim the final useless space. */
824:     sdsrange(rules,0,-2);
825: 
826:     /* This is technically not needed, but we want to verify that now the
827:      * predicted bitmap is exactly the same as the user bitmap, and abort
828:      * otherwise, because aborting is better than a security risk in this
829:      * code path. */
830:     if (memcmp(fake_selector->allowed_commands,
831:                         selector->allowed_commands,
832:                         sizeof(selector->allowed_commands)) != 0)
833:     {
834:         serverLog(LL_WARNING,
835:             "CRITICAL ERROR: User ACLs don't match final bitmap: '%s'",
836:             rules);
837:         serverPanic("No bitmap match in ACLDescribeSelectorCommandRules()");
838:     }
839:     ACLFreeSelector(fake_selector);
840:     return rules;
841: }

973: void ACLAddAllowedFirstArg(aclSelector *selector, unsigned long id, const char *sub) {
974:     /* If this is the first first-arg to be configured for
975:      * this user, we have to allocate the first-args array. */
976:     if (selector->allowed_firstargs == NULL) {
977:         selector->allowed_firstargs = zcalloc(USER_COMMAND_BITS_COUNT * sizeof(sds*));
978:     }
979: 
980:     /* We also need to enlarge the allocation pointing to the
981:      * null terminated SDS array, to make space for this one.
982:      * To start check the current size, and while we are here
983:      * make sure the first-arg is not already specified inside. */
984:     long items = 0;
985:     if (selector->allowed_firstargs[id]) {
986:         while(selector->allowed_firstargs[id][items]) {
987:             /* If it's already here do not add it again. */
988:             if (!strcasecmp(selector->allowed_firstargs[id][items],sub))
989:                 return;
990:             items++;
991:         }
992:     }
993: 
994:     /* Now we can make space for the new item (and the null term). */
995:     items += 2;
996:     selector->allowed_firstargs[id] = zrealloc(selector->allowed_firstargs[id], sizeof(sds)*items);
997:     selector->allowed_firstargs[id][items-2] = sdsnew(sub);
998:     selector->allowed_firstargs[id][items-1] = NULL;

1028: /* Set a selector's properties with the provided 'op'.
1029:  *
1030:  * +<command>   Allow the execution of that command.
1031:  *              May be used with `|` for allowing subcommands (e.g "+config|get")
1032:  * -<command>   Disallow the execution of that command.
1033:  *              May be used with `|` for blocking subcommands (e.g "-config|set")
1034:  * +@<category> Allow the execution of all the commands in such category
1035:  *              with valid categories are like @admin, @set, @sortedset, ...
1036:  *              and so forth, see the full list in the server.c file where
1037:  *              the Redis command table is described and defined.
1038:  *              The special category @all means all the commands, but currently
1039:  *              present in the server, and that will be loaded in the future
1040:  *              via modules.
1041:  * +<command>|first-arg    Allow a specific first argument of an otherwise
1042:  *                         disabled command. Note that this form is not
1043:  *                         allowed as negative like -SELECT|1, but
1044:  *                         only additive starting with "+".
1045:  * allcommands  Alias for +@all. Note that it implies the ability to execute
1046:  *              all the future commands loaded via the modules system.
1047:  * nocommands   Alias for -@all.
1048:  * ~<pattern>   Add a pattern of keys that can be mentioned as part of
1049:  *              commands. For instance ~* allows all the keys. The pattern
1050:  *              is a glob-style pattern like the one of KEYS.
1051:  *              It is possible to specify multiple patterns.
1052:  * %R~<pattern> Add key read pattern that specifies which keys can be read
1053:  *              from.
1054:  * %W~<pattern> Add key write pattern that specifies which keys can be
1055:  *              written to.
1056:  * allkeys      Alias for ~*
1057:  * resetkeys    Flush the list of allowed keys patterns.
1058:  * &<pattern>   Add a pattern of channels that can be mentioned as part of
1059:  *              Pub/Sub commands. For instance &* allows all the channels. The
1060:  *              pattern is a glob-style pattern like the one of PSUBSCRIBE.
1061:  *              It is possible to specify multiple patterns.
1062:  * allchannels              Alias for &*
1063:  * resetchannels            Flush the list of allowed channel patterns.
1064:  */
1065: int ACLSetSelector(aclSelector *selector, const char* op, size_t oplen) {
1066:     size_t viewlen = oplen;
1067:     if (op != NULL && viewlen == (size_t)-1) viewlen = strlen(op);
1068:     ACLSelectorApplyRulePolicy(selector, op, viewlen);
1069:     ACLSelectorApplyConfigPolicy(selector, op, viewlen);
1070:     if (!strcasecmp(op,"allkeys") ||
1071:                !strcasecmp(op,"~*"))
1072:     {
1073:         selector->flags |= SELECTOR_FLAG_ALLKEYS;
1074:         listEmpty(selector->patterns);
1075:     } else if (!strcasecmp(op,"resetkeys")) {
1076:         selector->flags &= ~SELECTOR_FLAG_ALLKEYS;
1077:         listEmpty(selector->patterns);
1078:     } else if (!strcasecmp(op,"allchannels") ||
1079:                !strcasecmp(op,"&*"))
1080:     {
1081:         selector->flags |= SELECTOR_FLAG_ALLCHANNELS;
1082:         listEmpty(selector->channels);
1083:     } else if (!strcasecmp(op,"resetchannels")) {
1084:         selector->flags &= ~SELECTOR_FLAG_ALLCHANNELS;
1085:         listEmpty(selector->channels);
1086:     } else if (!strcasecmp(op,"allcommands") ||
1087:                !strcasecmp(op,"+@all"))
1088:     {
1089:         memset(selector->allowed_commands,255,sizeof(selector->allowed_commands));
1090:         selector->flags |= SELECTOR_FLAG_ALLCOMMANDS;
1091:         sdsclear(selector->command_rules);
1092:         ACLResetFirstArgs(selector);
1093:     } else if (!strcasecmp(op,"nocommands") ||
1094:                !strcasecmp(op,"-@all"))
1095:     {
1096:         memset(selector->allowed_commands,0,sizeof(selector->allowed_commands));
1097:         selector->flags &= ~SELECTOR_FLAG_ALLCOMMANDS;
1098:         sdsclear(selector->command_rules);
1099:         ACLResetFirstArgs(selector);
1100:     } else if (op[0] == '~' || op[0] == '%') {
1101:         if (selector->flags & SELECTOR_FLAG_ALLKEYS) {
1102:             errno = EEXIST;
1103:             return C_ERR;
1104:         }
1105:         int flags = 0;
1106:         size_t offset = 1;
1107:         if (op[0] == '%') {
1108:             for (; offset < oplen; offset++) {
1109:                 if (toupper(op[offset]) == 'R' && !(flags & ACL_READ_PERMISSION)) {
1110:                     flags |= ACL_READ_PERMISSION;
1111:                 } else if (toupper(op[offset]) == 'W' && !(flags & ACL_WRITE_PERMISSION)) {
1112:                     flags |= ACL_WRITE_PERMISSION;
1113:                 } else if (op[offset] == '~') {
1114:                     offset++;

1118:                     return C_ERR;

1120:             }
1121:         } else {

1123:         }

1125:         if (ACLStringHasSpaces(op+offset,oplen-offset)) {

1128:         }

1241: /* Set user properties according to the string "op". The following
1242:  * is a description of what different strings will do:
1243:  *
1244:  * on           Enable the user: it is possible to authenticate as this user.
1245:  * off          Disable the user: it's no longer possible to authenticate
1246:  *              with this user, however the already authenticated connections
1247:  *              will still work.
1248:  * skip-sanitize-payload    RESTORE dump-payload sanitization is skipped.
1249:  * sanitize-payload         RESTORE dump-payload is sanitized (default).
1250:  * ><password>  Add this password to the list of valid password for the user.
1251:  *              For example >mypass will add "mypass" to the list.
1252:  *              This directive clears the "nopass" flag (see later).
1253:  * #<hash>      Add this password hash to the list of valid hashes for
1254:  *              the user. This is useful if you have previously computed
1255:  *              the hash, and don't want to store it in plaintext.
1256:  *              This directive clears the "nopass" flag (see later).
1257:  * <<password>  Remove this password from the list of valid passwords.
1258:  * !<hash>      Remove this hashed password from the list of valid passwords.
1259:  *              This is useful when you want to remove a password just by
1260:  *              hash without knowing its plaintext version at all.
1261:  * nopass       All the set passwords of the user are removed, and the user
1262:  *              is flagged as requiring no password: it means that every
1263:  *              password will work against this user. If this directive is
1264:  *              used for the default user, every new connection will be
1265:  *              immediately authenticated with the default user without
1266:  *              any explicit AUTH command required. Note that the "resetpass"
1267:  *              directive will clear this condition.
1268:  * resetpass    Flush the list of allowed passwords. Moreover removes the
1269:  *              "nopass" status. After "resetpass" the user has no associated
1270:  *              passwords and there is no way to authenticate without adding
